RESETTLEMENT POLICY FRAMEWORK (RPF)

Government of Grenada/World Bank Disaster Vulnerability Reduction Project (WB-GOG DVRP)

Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF) - Rationale

This Resettlement Policy Famework is an instrument which derives from the World Bank's Involuntary] Resettlement Policy (OP 4.12). OP 4.12 and covers direct economic and social impacts that both result

from Bank-assisted investment projects and are caused by:

(a) the involuntary taking of land resulting in

relocation or loss of shelter;

(i)

loss of assets or access to assets; or

(ii)

(iii)

loss of income sources or means of livelihood, whether or not the affected

persons must move to another location; or

[Context: persons must move to another location; or]
(b) The involuntary restriction of access to legally designated parks and protected areas resulting in

adverse impacts on the livelihoods of the displaced persons.

During project preparation of the Regional Disaster Vulnerability Project (RDVRP) it was determined

[Context: During project preparation of the Regional Disaster Vulnerability Project (RDVRP) it was determined]
that proposed project activities would likely lead to the involuntary acquisition of land. As a result the
Involuntary Resettlement Safeguard was triggered and an RPF prepared. The original RPF was disclosed

in April 2011 prior to the appraisal of the DVRP.
